- graphify: Use for any question about a codebase, its architecture, file relationships, or project content — especially when graphify-out/ exists, where the question should be treated as a graphify query first. Turns any input (code, docs, papers, images, videos) into a persistent knowledge graph with god nodes, community detection, and query/path/explain tools.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a GitHub pull request; for your working diff use /code-review
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

Perfect! Now I have a comprehensive picture of the markdown architecture. Let me compile my findings:

## Summary of Markdown Processing Architecture

Based on my thorough search of the codebase, here's the comprehensive markdown processing interface and implementation architecture:

### Core Interface: `ReactMarkdownProps`
**Location:** `/bench/home/work/web/src/components/MemoContent/markdown/types.ts`

```typescript
export interface ReactMarkdownProps {
  node?: Element;  // HAST node for advanced use cases
}
```

This is the foundational interface passed by react-markdown to all custom components.

### Main Renderer: `MemoMarkdownRenderer`
**Location:** `/bench/home/work/web/src/components/MemoContent/MemoMarkdownRenderer.tsx`

- **Interface:** `MemoMarkdownRendererProps`
  - `content: string` - markdown content to render
  - `resolvedMentionUsernames: Set<string>` - resolved mention usernames
  - `memoName?: string` - resource name for footnote links
  - `compact?: boolean` - rendering context flag

- **Core Architecture:** Uses React's `react-markdown` with customized component mappings via the `Components` type from react-markdown

### Context System: `MarkdownRenderContext`
**Location:** `/bench/home/work/web/src/components/MemoContent/MarkdownRenderContext.tsx`

```typescript
interface MarkdownRenderContextValue {
  blockDepth: number;
}
```

- Tracks nesting depth for block elements (blockquotes, lists)
- Provides `NestedMarkdownRenderContext` provider wrapper
- Hook: `useMarkdownRenderContext()` for accessing context in components

### Markdown Element Components (All extend `ReactMarkdownProps`)

**In `/bench/home/work/web/src/components/MemoContent/markdown/`:**
- `Heading.tsx` - h1-h6 elements
- `Paragraph.tsx` - paragraph elements with nesting context
- `Blockquote.tsx` - blockquote with nesting context
- `HorizontalRule.tsx` - hr elements
- `List.tsx` - ul/ol lists with task list support
- `Link.tsx` - external links
- `AnchorLink.tsx` - in-page anchor links
- `Image.tsx` - image elements
- `InlineCode.tsx` - inline code

**In parent directory:**
- `CodeBlock.tsx` - code blocks with syntax highlighting (highlight.js)
- `Table.tsx` - table elements (table, thead, tbody, tr, th, td)
- `TaskListItem.tsx` - checkbox input for task lists
- `Mention.tsx` - mention spans (@username)
- `Tag.tsx` - tag spans (#tagname)
- `TrustedIframe.ts` - iframe elements

### Custom Remark Plugins (Markdown AST transformations)
**Location:** `/bench/home/work/web/src/utils/remark-plugins/`

1. **`remark-mention.ts`** - Parses and creates mention nodes
   - Functions: `parseMentionsFromText()`, `extractMentionUsernames()`
   - Creates `MentionNode` objects (custom AST nodes)

2. **`remark-tag.ts`** - Parses and creates tag nodes
   - Handles backslash escaping for tags
   - Creates `TagNode` objects (custom AST nodes)
   - Respects backslash escaping per CommonMark spec

3. **`remark-disable-setext.ts`** - Disables setext (underline-style) headings

4. **`remark-split-mixed-task-lists.ts`** - Splits mixed task/regular lists into separate lists

5. **`remark-preserve-type.ts`** - Preserves custom node types via `mdastType` in node data

### Custom Rehype Plugins (HTML transformation)
**Location:** `/bench/home/work/web/src/utils/rehype-plugins/`

1. **`rehype-heading-id.ts`** - Adds unique slugified `id` attributes to h1-h6 headings

### Type System Extensions
**Location:** `/bench/home/work/web/src/types/markdown.ts`

```typescript
export interface TagNode { type: "tagNode"; value: string; data: TagNodeData; }
export interface MentionNode { type: "mentionNode"; value: string; data: MentionNodeData; }
export interface ExtendedData extends Data { mdastType?: string; }

// Type guard functions:
- isTagElement(node: HastElement): boolean
- isMentionElement(node: HastElement): boolean
- isTaskListItemElement(node: HastElement): boolean
```

### Utility Functions
**Location:** `/bench/home/work/web/src/utils/markdown-manipulation.ts`

- `toggleTaskAtLine()`, `toggleTaskAtIndex()` - Update task list state
- `countTasks()` - Count total/completed/incomplete tasks
- `extractHeadings()` - Extract h1-h4 headings with slugs
- `extractTasks()` - Extract task list items with metadata
- `getTaskLineNumber()` - Get line number of task by index
- `slugify()` - Convert text to URL-friendly anchors

**Location:** `/bench/home/work/web/src/utils/markdown-task-actions.ts`
- `MarkdownEdit` interface - Source range edits
- Task parsing and manipulation utilities

### Entry Point & Consumer
**Location:** `/bench/home/work/web/src/components/MemoContent/index.tsx`

- Exports `MemoContent` component (default export)
- Interface: `MemoContentProps`
- Instantiates `MemoMarkdownRenderer` with resolved mention usernames
- Wraps renderer in context provider with root `MarkdownRenderContext`

### External Dependencies
The system integrates:
- `react-markdown` - Core markdown-to-React rendering
- `remark-*` plugins (remark-breaks, remark-gfm, remark-math)
- `rehype-*` plugins (rehype-raw, rehype-sanitize, rehype-katex)
- `unist-util-visit` - AST traversal
- `mdast-util-*` - Markdown AST utilities
- `micromark` - Markdown parsing
- `highlight.js` - Syntax highlighting
- `KaTeX` - Math rendering

### Data Flow
1. Raw markdown content arrives at `MemoContent`
2. Mention usernames extracted via `extractMentionUsernames()`
3. `MemoMarkdownRenderer` receives content + resolved mentions
4. Remark plugins transform markdown AST (mentions, tags, task lists, etc.)
5. Rehype plugins transform HTML AST (heading IDs, sanitization, math)
6. React-markdown renders with customized component map
7. Each component receives `ReactMarkdownProps` with HAST node reference
8. Context providers enable nesting depth tracking for block elements
